1 Important Information for Tentative Rulings and Hearings:
1. Please review and follow the Tentative Ruling Instructions which can be found on the Court’s website
using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/divisions/unified-family-court/ufc-tentative-rulings.
2. If you wish to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, you must notify the other party
(unless there is a restraining order in place) and the Court Clerk in the Department where the hearing
is scheduled of your objection by 4:00 PM the Court day prior to the hearing date. Court days do not
include Court holidays, Saturdays, or Sundays. The Court’s Holiday Schedule can be found on the
Court’s website using the following link: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/general-information/holiday-
schedules.
3. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 403 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551–3741 or send an email to Department403@sftc.org.
4. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 404 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551–3744 or send an email to Department404@sftc.org.
5. To contact the Court Clerk in Dept. 416 to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case,
please call (415) 551– 3756 or send an email to Department416@sftc.org.
6. When you contact the Court Clerk to make an objection to the Tentative Ruling in your case, please
specify the paragraph(s) and / or line number(s) of the Tentative Ruling which contains the language
to which you object.
7. You may appear at your hearing either (a) in-person; (b) by video; or (c) by phone. Pursuant to SFLR
11.7(D)(4), if you choose to appear by video or phone, you must be continuously connected to Zoom
from 8:50 a.m. until 12:00 p.m. or until your hearing is concluded (or from 1:20 p.m. until 4:30 p.m.
or until your hearing is concluded, if your hearing is scheduled to start at 1:30 p.m.). If you fail to
appear in-person, by video, or phone, the Court may proceed with the hearing in your absence. The
Court is not required to contact you before your hearing.
8. If you choose to appear by video or by phone, you must comply with the Notice and Instructions for
Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth below.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER RE: ENTRY OF JUDGMENTE ON COURT-ORDERED ARREARS
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner Fernand Farol and Respondent Lissa Q. Farol.
18 2) On 1/12/26, Respondent filed a Request for Order seeking entry of judgment on child support
19 add-on expense arrears pursuant to the Court’s 9/26/24 Findings and Order After Hearing
20 (FOAH). On 9/26/24, the Court ordered Petitioner to pay Respondent $28,063.36 for the three
21 minor children’s unreimbursed medical expenses in 12 equal payments commencing on 10/15/24
22 and continuing the 15th of every month thereafter (until the balance is paid in full). Attached to
23 Respondent’s Request for Order is form FL-490 (Application to Determine Arrears).
24 3) There is no proof of service on file indicating Respondent’s 1/12/26 Request for Order was
25 served on Petitioner.
26 4) The Court notes that on 12/10/24, DCSS filed a notice (Notice Regarding Payment of Support
27 (NRPS)) advising of San Mateo DCCS’ involvement in the case.
28 B. Findings and Order
1 1) The Court finds Respondent’s 1/12/26 Request for Order was not served at least 16 Court days
2 prior to the hearing date as required by Code of Civil Procedure section 1005(b).
3 2) As such, this matter is CONTINUED to 5/2/26 at 9 AM in Dept. 414 for (a) lack of service and
4 (b) because DCSS is involved in the case, so the matter must be heard in Dept. 414 (and cannot
5 be heard in Dept. 403).
6 3) At least 20 calendar days prior to the next Court hearing, Respondent shall file and serve on
7 Petitioner the (a) Request for Order, (b) Continuance Order contained herein, and
8 (c) Tentative Ruling Instructions using a service method authorized by the Code of Civil
9 Procedure.
10 4) At least 9 calendar days prior to the next Court hearing, Petitioner may file a Responsive
11 Declaration.
12 5) At least 5 Court days prior to the next hearing date, Respondent may file and serve a Reply
13 Declaration.
14 6) Respondent is encouraged to seek assistance from the ACCESS Center if needed. Information for
15 contacting the ACCESS Center can be found here: https://sf.courts.ca.gov/access-legal-self-help-
16 center.
17 7) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER FOR CHANGE OF CHILD CUSTODY, VISITATION (PARENTING TIME),
13 ORDER SHORTENING TIME
14 TENTATIVE RULING
15 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
16 Court makes the following findings and orders:
17 A. Procedural History
18 1) The parties are Petitioner Tim Ngo (Father) and Respondent Li Xu (Mother). The minor children
19 subject to this proceeding are Seraphina Ngo (DPB: 06/01/08) and Saphira Ngo (DOB; 08/27/12).
20 2) On January 30, 2026, Father filed an ex parte application seeking emergency orders for custody
21 and visitation alleging both minor children are afraid of Mother’s boyfriend, Gary Ivan, and that
22 he has been abusive to them. Father asserts that the minor children do not want to visit Mother
23 while her boyfriend is present. Father seeks the following orders:
24 a. Sole legal and sole physical custody of the minor children.
25 b. Suspension of Mother’s parenting time.
26 c. A Family Court Services (FCS) Tier II interview of school counselor Sharon Kwan.
27 3) On January 30, 2026, the Court granted Father’s emergency request. The Court awarded Father
28 temporary custody of both minor children and suspended Mother’s visitation.
1 4) On February 5, 2026, Mother filed a Responsive Declaration, which the Court read and
2 considered.
3 5) On February 9, 2026 (at the Court’s Readiness Hearing), the Court referred the parties to FCS
4 mediation on March 24, 2026 and set a return hearing on March 24, 2026.
5 B. Findings and Order
6 1) This Court has jurisdiction to make child custody orders in this case under the Uniform Child
7 Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act. A violation of this order may subject the party in
8 violation to civil or criminal penalties, or both. The country of habitual residence of the minor
9 child is the United States.
10 2) Father shall continue to have temporary sole legal and sole physical custody of both minor
11 children.
12 3) Mother’s parenting time with the minor child Seraphia Ngo (06/01/08) shall be at the minor
13 child’s discretion.
14 4) Mother’s parenting time with the minor child Saphira Ngo (08/27/12) shall be every Saturday and
15 Sunday from 10:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
16 5) The matter is referred to FCS for a Tier II interview of the minor children to determine whether
17 there is any physical, verbal, or emotional abuse at Mother’s home.
18 6) Mother’s partner, Gary Ivan, shall NOT be present during ANY time when the minor children
19 have parenting time with Mother. Mother shall ensure that Gary Ivan is not present. Gary Ivan’s
20 presence during Mother’s parenting time will result in immediate suspension of Mother’s
21 parenting time.
22 7) The matter is continued to May 19, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. in Dept. 403 for review of the Tier II
23 report.
24 8) All existing orders, not in conflict with the orders made herein, shall remain in full force and
25 effect.
26 9) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 OTHER REVIEW HEARING
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties in this matter are Petitioner Katherine Mlika (Mother) and Respondent Zdenek Mlika
18 (Father). The parties married on 9/8/2012. Their agreed-upon date of separation is 4/30/2021, for
19 a marriage of 8 years and 7 months. The parties share equal timeshare of their children Peter
20 (DOB: 8/17/2014) and Robert (DOB: 3/25/2017).
21 2) On 3/19/2024, a Stipulated Judgment was entered which requires Mother to pay Father $1,636
22 per month in guideline child support and $1,800 per month in long-term spousal support (which is
23 set to decrease by $200 every 12 months until Mother has paid spousal support for 36 months at
24 which time Mother’s obligation to pay spousal support to Father shall terminate). Paragraph 7(f)
25 of the Judgment states: “The amount of spousal support as provided herein shall be modifiable
26 downward based upon a material change of circumstance.” The support orders are based on
27 Father’s earning $3,132 per month and Mother’s earning $15,292 per month.
1 3) On 12/24/2024, Mother filed a Request for Order seeking modification of child and spousal
2 support to $0. Mother stated that her government contract ended on 11/6/2024 and she was
3 searching for new employment.
4 4) At the prior 5/13/2025 hearing (per the Findings and Order After Hearing filed 8/1/2025), the
5 Court ordered Mother to pay to Father $8,000 for a remaining balance owed to him under the
6 parties’ Judgment in increments of $2,000 per month commencing 6/15/2025, ordered Mother to
7 spend at least 20 hours per week searching for a position of paid employment commensurate with
8 her earning capacity, and continued the hearing on Mother’s request to modify child and spousal
9 support to 8/5/2025.
10 5) At the 8/5/2025 hearing, the Court ordered Mother to pay to Father 50% of the previously ordered
11 support amount (i.e., $1,718 per month) and set a second review hearing for 10/21/2025.
12 6) On 9/30/2025, Mother filed two declarations, one wherein she details payments to Father between
13 1/7/2025 and 9/15/2025 and the second wherein Mother details her job search efforts since
14 November 2024 (when her prior contract ended). Mother reports that she regularly deducts
15 expenses for the parties’ children and Father’s life insurance fees from payments to Father.
16 Mother states that she has applied to approximately 60 roles at a range of small and large tech
17 companies.
18 7) On 9/30/2025, Mother filed an Income and Expense Declaration. Mother states that she began a
19 position as a contractor on 8/25/2025 working 16 hours per week and earns $100 per hour.
20 Mother states that her average monthly income totals $6,600 in gross per month. Mother states
21 that her monthly expenses total $11,884 (which includes $2,708 in carrying costs for her home,
22 $2,000 per month to pay down a HELOC, and $1,419 per month to pay down credit card debts
23 and other loans). Mother reports having $2,000 in cash and $280,000 in real property equity. In
24 addition to owing $243,389 on a HELOC, Mother reports owing $86,158 in credit card debt and
25 other loans.
26 8) On 10/14/2025, Father filed an Income and Expense Declaration. Father states that he earns $100
27 per month through occasional work at restaurants and $1,000 per month in self-employment
28 income through his boat renovation business. Father states that he has been working less due to
29 enrollment in a Diagnostic Medical Imaging program at CCSF, with an expected graduation date
1 of 2028 – 2029. Father states that his monthly expenses total $6,130, but his parents give him
2 $600 per month in assistance. Father states that he has $980 in cash and owns personal property
3 worth less than $5,000. Father reports owing $11,970 in credit card debt. Father states, “Due to
4 the 50% decrease in support for the last few months I am already facing increased credit card debt
5 and I will soon start to struggle to make basic monthly cash payments.”
6 9) At the prior 10/21/2025 hearing, the Court ordered, in pertinent part:
7 a. The prior orders requiring Mother to pay Father $1,780 per month in child and spousal
8 support and for Mother to spend at least 20 hours per week searching for employment
9 shall remain in full force and effect.
10 b. The Court will set another review hearing on Thursday, 1/15/2026 at 9:00 AM in Dept.
11 403.
12 c. At least 10 calendar days prior to the next hearing date, Mother shall file and serve a
13 declaration summarizing her work search efforts since 10/1/2025 and her payments to
14 Father since 9/15/2025. Mother shall also file and serve an updated Income and Expense
15 Declaration.
16 d. At least 10 calendar days prior to the next hearing date, Father shall file and serve an
17 updated Income and Expense Declaration.
18 e. If either party wishes the Court to make any new orders at the next hearing date regarding
19 child and spousal support, they must file and serve a declaration a declaration at least 20
20 calendar days prior to the next hearing date and the other party may file and serve a
21 declaration responding to that request at least 10 calendar days prior to the next hearing
22 date.
23 10) On 1/5/2026, the parties filed an Agreement and Order to Reschedule Hearing; the 1/15/2025
24 review hearing was rescheduled to 3/24/2026.
25 11) On 3/5/2026, Father filed an Income and Expense Declaration indicating his average monthly
26 self-employment income is $741.50 plus $197 for occasional work at a restaurant. Father lists
27 $302,420 in cash assets, and states his personal property is worth less than $5,000 and his current
28 debt is $15,975.36. Father indicates his average monthly expenses are $6,256, $600 of which are
29 paid by others. Father states he pays $85 monthly for children’s healthcare not covered by
1 insurance and Mother subtracted $1,010 from child support payments as 50% of reimbursement
2 for children’s orthodontia, speech therapy, and summer camp.
3 12) On 3/13/2026, Mother filed an Income and Expense Declaration indicating she earns $16,333 in
4 average monthly income, pays $600 in monthly health insurance premiums, has $2,000 in cash
5 assets, has $300,300 in real and personal property, and pays $13,898 in average monthly
6 expenses. Mother lists $340,000 in debt, $251,000 of which is a HELOC. Mother indicates she
7 pays $400 monthly for children’s healthcare not covered by insurance.
8 13) On 3/13/2026, Mother filed a declaration detailing the child support and spousal support
9 payments she made from 9/15/2026 – 3/10/2026. Mother states she paid Father $7,023.30
10 therefore she is up to date on payments through February. Mother indicates she has not paid
11 Father the $8,000 lump sum.
12 14) The Court notes that neither party requested that the Court make any orders at the 3/24/2026
13 hearing.
14 B. Findings and Order
15 1) Given that Mother’s Income and Expense Declaration filed 3/13/2026, and signed under penalty
16 of perjury, indicates that she secured full time employment as of 1/12/2026, the Court finds good
17 cause to VACATE the seek work order on Mother and modify child support and spousal support
18 based on a material change in circumstances (i.e., Mother securing full-time employment) as
19 follows:
20 2) Effective 3/1/2026, Mother shall pay Father pursuant to the terms of the 3/19/2024 Stipulated
21 Judgment, which requires Mother to pay Father $1,636 per month in guideline child support and
22 $1,800 per month in long-term spousal support (which is set to decrease by $200 every 12 months
23 until Mother has paid spousal support for 36 months at which time Mother’s obligation to pay
24 spousal support to Father shall terminate).
25 3) Additionally, on 5/13/2025 the Court ordered Mother to pay to Father $8,000 for a remaining
26 balance owed to him under the parties’ Judgment in increments of $2,000 per month commencing
27 6/15/2025. See Findings and Order After Hearing (FOAH) filed 8/1/2025. In her 3/13/2026
28 declaration. Mother states she has not paid Father $8,000 lump sum. Mother is admonished for
1 failing to comply with the Court’s 5/13/2025 order and warned that legal interest accrues on
2 overdue payments.
3 4) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 REQUEST FOR ORDER: CONTEMPT AND MONETARY SANCTIONS
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Having read and considered the pleadings, declarations, and other evidence submitted in this matter, the
15 Court makes the following findings and orders:
16 A. Procedural History
17 1) The parties are Petitioner Danielle Schmid-Maybach (Mother) and Respondent Ulrich Schmid-
18 Maybach (Father).
19 2) On 11/10/25, Dissolution Judgment was entered incorporating a Memorandum of Understanding
20 (MOU) signed by the parties on 2/6/25. See Judgment file dated 11/12/25.
21 3) On 11/18/25, Mother filed an Order to Show Cause Re: Contempt alleging Father violated the
22 terms of the parties’ 2/6/25 MOU by failing to transfer title of the 2012 Mercedes to Mother. The
23 Court notes this Order to Show Cause Re: Contempt is file stamped 11/18/25 on the document,
24 but file dated 11/20/25 on the Court’s docket. The matter was set for hearing on 2/5/26.
25 4) On 1/5/26, Mother filed a Request for Order seeking: (a) a finding of contempt for Father’s
26 noncompliance with judgment terms, including transfer of title of the 2012 Mercedes to Mother;
27 (b) $20,900 in reimbursements for unavoidable costs incurred due to Father’s noncompliance,
28 including car rental expenses, a Tesla lease down payment and monthly lease costs, fees for legal
29 document preparation and attorney consultation, and other costs incurred; (c) $10,000 in
1 monetary sanctions; and (d) immediate compliance or appointment of the Court Clerk as elisor
2 sign the documents necessary effectuate transfer of title on Father’s behalf. Mother asserts she is
3 the parent responsible for transporting the parties’ minor child to and from visitation with Father,
4 and Father’s continued refusal to transfer title of the 2012 Mercedes caused Mother to incur
5 substantial expenses and put the minor child’s safety at risk. The matter is set for hearing on
6 3/24/26.
7 5) On 1/5/26, Mother filed a Proof of Electronic Service indicating service of her 1/5/26 Request for
8 Order was effectuated on 1/5/26.
9 6) On 2/5/26, the parties appeared at hearing during which Father agreed to 2/5/26 as the date of
10 service of Mother’s 11/18/25 Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt. The Court
11 continued the matter to 4/28/26 at 9 AM in Dept. 403
12 7) Father did not file a Responsive Declaration to Mother’s 1/5/26 Request for Order.
13 B. Findings and Order
14 1) Mother’s request for a finding of contempt is DENIED as the request is procedurally defective.
15 2) Mother’s request for $20,900 in reimbursements for unavoidable costs incurred due to Father’s
16 alleged noncompliance, including car rental expenses, a Tesla lease down payment and monthly
17 lease costs, fees for legal document preparation and attorney consultation, and other costs
18 incurred is DENIED as the request is unsupported by any documentary evidence.
19 3) The Court confirms that the 11/10/25 Dissolution Judgment, which incorporates a Memorandum
20 of Understanding (MOU) signed by the parties on 2/6/25, confirms the 2017 Smart Car and 2012
21 Mercedes to Mother as her sole and separate property. See Judgment file dated 11/12/25.
22 However, the Court finds that the Judgment lacks orders effectuating the transfer of title.
23 4) Based on the foregoing, the Court finds good cause to order Father to sign all necessary
24 documents to execute the transfer of title of the 2012 Mercedes to Mother by 4/28/26.
25 5) The Court reserves jurisdiction over Mother’s request for appointment of the Court Clerk as elisor
26 to sign the documents necessary effectuate transfer of title on Father’s behalf.
27 6) The Court also reserves jurisdiction over Mother’s request for $10,000 in monetary sanctions.
28 The Court would be inclined to grant such a request pursuant to code of Civil Procedure section
29 271 should Father fail to meet the 4/28/26 deadline set forth above.
1 7) The Court will prepare the Findings and Order After Hearing.

12 ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE AND AFFIDAVIT FOR CONTEMPT
13 TENTATIVE RULING
14 Appearances required. The parties may appear in person in Dept. 403 or remotely by Zoom video.
15 If a party chooses to appear by video, that party must abide by the Notice and Instructions for
16 Remote Appearances in San Francisco Family Court set forth above.
17 1) On for hearing is Petitioner Marina Baran’s Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt filed
18 10/28/25 alleging that Respondent Alexander Baran violated a Stipulation and Order filed 10/14/25
19 providing Petitioner with one week per month of custody of the family dog, Lexi.
20 2) On 12/12/25, Petitioner filed a Proof of Service by Mail indicating Petitioner’s 10/28/25
21 Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt was served on Respondent by mail on 12/12/25.
22 3) At the prior 12/30/25 hearing, both parties appeared in pro per and were sworn and examined. The
23 Court issued the following orders:
24 a. Petitioner is granted visitation with the family dog, Lexi, three days per week starting
25 12/30/25 at noon and ending 1/2/26 at noon. Thereafter, the parties shall return to the original
26 visitation schedule ordered (in the Stipulation and Order filed 10/14/25).
27 b. Per Cedars-Sinai Imaging Medical Group v. Superior Court (2000) 83 Cal.App.4th 1281,
28 personal service of an Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt-on-contempt citee is
29 required.
1 c. As such, the hearing on Petitioner’s Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt filed
2 10/28/25 is hereby continued to 3/24/26 at 9:00 AM in Dept. 403 to permit Petitioner time to
3 effectuate proper service.
4 d. Petitioner shall have a third-party, 18 years of age or older, personally serve Respondent with
5 the Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt filed 10/28/25 at least 30 calendar days
6 prior to the next hearing date.
7 4) On 12/30/25, Petitioner filed a Proof of Personal Service indicating Respondent was served at the
8 courthouse on 12/30/25.
9 5) The Court notes Petitioner also filed (a) an Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for Contempt on
10 1/29/26, which is set for hearing on 4/21/26; and (b) an Order to Show Cause and Affidavit for
11 Contempt on 2/18/26, which is set for hearing on 4/21/26. Petitioner asserts that Respondent
12 continues to withhold the family dog, Lexi, in violation of Court orders.
13 6) The parties are ordered to appear. Respondent shall be prepared to inform the Court whether he
14 would like contempt counsel appointed to represent him in this contempt action. If Respondent would
15 like contempt counsel appointed, Respondent must file an Income and Expense Declaration for the
16 Court to determine whether he qualifies, and then Court will set a future hearing date for appointment
17 of contempt counsel and Respondent’s arraignment. If Respondent does not want contempt counsel to
18 be appointed, the Court will arraign Respondent at the 3/24/26 hearing and set a future trial date.
